thread:
sam: Heads-up — saw a tail-latency regression after yesterday's coalesce jitter seed tweak. p95 for small-seq workloads jumped from 42ms -> 130ms on canary.

jess: ugh, that's big. which change exactly? the new randomized coalesce seed PR? :eyes: 

sam: yeah PR #4045. We randomized microbatch slot offset per-request to reduce sync phases. Intended to smooth arrival clustering. Metrics: 10% throughput up, but p95 spike on short sequences.

ravi: any kernel-selection correlation? might be picking a different attn kernel for slightly longer avg seq during the jitter window.

sam: good catch. profiler shows more invocations of attn_naive_fused for sequences 64-96 instead of attn_winograd_optimized. Attached snippet from trace:
```
metric: kernel_invocations
attn_winograd_optimized: 182k
attn_naive_fused: 94k -> 210k (canary)
kv_cache_evictions: 820 -> 4300
coalesce_delay_ms: 1.8 -> 3.6 (avg)
```

marta: kv evictions jumped too? that explains token re-computation pressure.

sam: yep. the randomized offset increases the observed sequence-length distribution at time of kernel selection + cache priming mismatch -> evictions. It's an emergent behavior.

nate: can we add a quick guard: when avg coalesce_delay < 5ms, prefer winograd kernel for <=96 tokens? should be cheap rule.

jess: or we can bias the seed distribution to keep mean offset low (reduce right tail) rather than full uniform. Less disruptive.

ravi: we should also add a trace tag to every request: chosen_coalesce_slot_seed and chosen_kernel_hint so we can correlate per-request. Right now it's only aggregate.

sam: +1. I'll push a tiny change to log seed and kernel_hint into trace span and add metrics. Also proposing an immediate rollback of seed randomness on canary while we iterate.

deploy-bot: deploy request submitted by sam for rollback to canary cluster: rollback coalesce-seed-rand (deploy/rollback) — started

marta: for longer term, we should evaluate kernel cost surface under microburst conditions in the kernel selector: simulate coalesce delay distribution and run pprof to pick stable kernels.

ravi: I'll produce a small workload generator to replay observed arrival patterns (script below). We can run autotune.
```
# short script sketch
for seed in 1 2 3 5 7; do
  ./coalesce-sim --seed=$seed --arrival-pattern=empirical.json --out=trace_$seed.pb
done
```

jess: thanks — once we have traces, we can run a compare job: p50/p95/p99 for each kernel with kv priming sim.

sam: timeline: 1) rollback canary now; 2) add trace fields & one-off generator; 3) run offline autotune with biased seed; 4) try mild seed bias rollout. I'll follow up with numbers by EOD.

nate: thanks Sam. also add alert: coalesce_delay_99 > 10ms or kv_cache_evictions_rate > 1k/min should page eng-runtime on call.

sam: noted. adding alerts now.

deploy-bot: rollback canary completed — service health steady. :white_check_mark: 

marta: nice. keep thread updated with perf comparison artifacts (pprof flamegraphs, kernel hit rates).
